rounds.text: Kopran Ltd benefits from powerful macro tailwinds with the healthcare sector registering a tailwind score of +0.80 to +0.90 [E74, E75]. The company demonstrates extraordinary price momentum, boasting a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a twelve-month price return of 48.4%, and a multi-year sales uptrend supported by recent 12% TTM sales growth [E17, E52, E53, E66]. Crucially, capital expenditure appears to have largely completed as evidenced by Capital Work in Progress dropping 77.9% to Rs 25 Cr, which signals new capacity coming online [E41]. This operational scaling is reinforced by exceptional cash generation, with cash conversion hitting 2.58x and operating cash flow reaching Rs 67 Cr—representing 117% of operating profit—while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.29x [E34, E35, E37, E38]. Furthermore, the company rewards shareholders with a healthy dividend payout of 40.8% and trades at a price-to-book ratio of 2.31x, which compares favorably to the sector benchmark of 2.85x [E2, E7, E60]. conceded: [E21] and [E46].

Kopran Ltd carries severe valuation risks, trading at an exorbitant P/E ratio of 48.6x to 49.1x against a sector benchmark of 32.16x, while its EV/EBITDA of 23.34x also outpaces the sector's 17.13x [E1, E6, E11]. This rich multiple rests on deteriorating fundamentals, highlighted by a -28% trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -16% [E19, E21]. Compounded share price growth of 5% over 5 years sharply lags behind price-led exuberance where the stock sits 76% to 80% of the way up its 52-year range and price growth exceeds profit growth by 73% recently [E5, E23, E49, E58]. Fundamental returns languish with an ROE of 4.9% and ROCE of 6.56% to 6.7%, severely underperforming sector benchmarks of 10.38% and 11.95% respectively [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, a DCF intrinsic value calculation of Rs 57 yields a staggering -338.6% margin of safety, with a reverse DCF implying an aggressive 20.4% earnings growth that completely disconnects from reality [E46, E47, E48]. Conceded: [E34], [E38], [E75].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E11], [E19], [E21], [E46], [E47], and [E48]. While the bear focuses on trailing profit contraction and rich headline multiples, it overlooks the powerful operational transformation underway as evidenced by capital expenditure coming online through a 77.9% drop in capital work-in-progress to Rs 25 Cr [E41]. This completed capex already drives top-line momentum, evidenced by a 12% trailing twelve-month sales growth and a recent 14% year-over-year sales increase [E17, E65]. The company's earnings power is securely backed by cash, boasting an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 2.58x where operating cash flow reached Rs 67 Cr and fully backed reported profits at 117% [E34, E35, E37]. Furthermore, the balance sheet remains soundly positioned with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.29x [E38], while the stock rides a massive sector tailwind in healthcare and a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E52, E75].

Conceded: [E41]. While capital work-in-progress dropped 77.9% [E41], this completed capex fails to translate into profit growth, as evidenced by a compounded profit contraction of -16% over 5 years and -28% over the trailing twelve months [E19, E21]. Although operating cash flow reached Rs 67 Cr [E35], the free cash flow for the exact same period stands at Rs -0 Cr [E36], revealing that the high operating cash conversion of 2.58x [E34] is entirely consumed by capital intensity or other outflows. The debt-to-equity ratio of 0.29x [E38] masks an absolute rise in borrowings to Rs 153 Cr from Rs 148 Cr [E40], alongside warning flags that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E63]. Furthermore, relying on the relative strength rating of 100 [E52] ignores the explicit price-led divergence where price growth exceeds profit growth by 73% [E58], leaving the stock vulnerable to a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -92.6% [E54].
